feedback.problem:
The total number of people $T(t)$ at a festival after $t$ hours is given by the function

$$
T(t)=10+{\int }_{0}^{t}2x-4\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $T$ is measured in thousands of people, and $t>0$ is the time (in hours) since the festival opened its gates.

At what time is the number of people at the festival a minimum, and how many people are at the festival at this time?
feedback.worked_solution:
To find when the number of people is at a minimum, we need to solve $\frac{\text{d}T}{\text{d}t}=0.$ First, we differentiate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}T}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2+{\int }_{0}^{t}2x-4\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({\int }_{0}^{t}2x-4\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}{\int }_{0}^{t}2x-4\,\text{d}x \\  & =2t-4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve $\frac{\text{d}T}{\text{d}t}=0$:

$$
2t-4=0\,⟹\,t=2
$$

So there are two candidates for global extrema, $t=0$ and $t=2.$ To find out how many people are in the festival when $t=2,$ we figure out $T(2)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(2) & =10+{\int }_{0}^{2}2x-4\,\text{d}x \\  & =10+{[{x}^{2}-4x]|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =10+[({2}^{2}-4(2))-(0)] \\  & =10-4 \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Since $6\,000<10\,000$, we conclude that the minimum number of people is $6\,000$, and this will happen after $2$ hours.

submitted_fields.submitted_value: The minimum is $6\,000$ people after $2$ hours
